title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division
source_system: ERP general ledger (SYS-G4); FY2025 Form 10-K segment note

title: Group: SYS-G1 authentication and sign-in policy export
source_system: Group identity platform admin console (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: About 45,000 workforce identities and about 2,100 outsourced agent identities, unique and never reused. MFA with number matching for all workforce and outsourced agent accounts, including NOC staff; phishing-resistant hardware keys for IT administrators; workforce accounts lock after 10 failed attempts; passwords of at least 14 characters checked against breached-password lists. IT applications in all three divisions federate to SYS-G1, including SYS-T1 through single sign-on

title: Group: identity governance export and Q1 2026 access certification results
source_system: Identity governance module (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows driven by HR events; the two outsourced contact center vendors send agent leavers in a weekly file. Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically, including outsourced agent accounts; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days; break-glass accounts are sealed and listed in a register. The Q1 2026 quarterly certification covered IT applications and privileged and CPNI-capable roles. Role requests and approvals are recorded per application

title: Group: privileged access management policy, session records and secrets vault report
source_system: Privileged access management console and secrets vault (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: IT administrators hold separate privileged accounts, elevated just in time with approval and session recording; vendor maintenance sessions to OSS/BSS components are brokered through PAM with named accounts; privileged session logs go to the SIEM. Integration secrets are held in the vault; 3 OSS and BSS integrations use static secrets older than 1 year

title: Group: endpoint baseline, zero-trust access and mobile access standard
source_system: Endpoint management console; zero-trust access gateway
what_it_shows: Managed endpoints lock after 10 minutes idle. Remote workforce access goes through the zero-trust access service with device checks and MFA; remote sessions use TLS 1.2 or higher or IPsec. Remote administration of OSS/BSS components is routed through the zero-trust service and regional jump hosts. The mobile access standard lets personal devices reach the BSS only through managed browsers

title: Group: SIEM data source inventory, use cases and log retention settings
source_system: Group SIEM (SYS-G2); log archive account
what_it_shows: 24x7 SOC. Logs are kept 1 year searchable and 6 years in an object-locked archive account that SOC and platform administrators cannot delete from. Sources include identity, PAM, cloud audit, EDR, the BSS, the OSS and AAA accounting from the legacy regions; use cases cover atypical BSS agent activity (bulk CDR views, after-hours searches, VIP lookups), bulk ticket exports from the service assurance platform, and large CDR transfers. Not in the source list: network element syslog and AAA logs from the 2 acquired regions (kept on regional collectors for 30 days), SYS-E1 gateway and collector logs (kept locally for 30 days), and RMU platform and smart lock logs (kept 90 days in the RMU platform)

title: Group: SOC playbooks, incident case export and exercise reports, April 2025 to March 2026
source_system: Group SOC case management system (SYS-G2); SOC document library
what_it_shows: Incidents are tracked in one case register that also serves as the CPNI breach record, under group playbooks and the group severity scale, with Carrier NOC and lawful-intercept liaisons named. The Tower division escalates on its own 3-level scale. The isolation playbooks for SBCs and the service assurance platform have no step that checks 911 or tower lighting effects first. Technical playbooks were exercised each quarter; no exercise covered cross-division notification

title: Group: vulnerability scan coverage and known-exploited remediation report, Q1 2026

CISA, FBI and vendor advisories are logged as tickets and assigned to owners

BSS agent sessions end after 30 minutes idle and OSS and element manager sessions after 15 minutes

title: Tower and Fiber Infrastructure: site, structure, RMU and smart lock inventory
source_system: SYS-T2 RMU and lock inventory; antenna structure registration records
what_it_shows: About 14,500 towers and 2,100 rooftop and in-building sites in 22 states, many in coastal areas; about 6,200 registered antenna structures with FAA lighting specifications, each monitored by an RMU, with tenants notified of registration. About 5,100 newer RMUs are certified under 47 CFR 17.47(c), use the private APN and support vendor direct alerting. About 1,100 legacy RMUs from the 2023 tower portfolio acquisition use cellular modems from a single cellular provider, with public IP addresses and shared credentials. Smart locks at about 9,000 sites; cameras at about 2,400 of them

title: Tower and Fiber Infrastructure: Alarm Monitoring Center procedures, contingency plan v2023 and outage records
source_system: Tower continuity library; alarm center procedures; outage record spreadsheets
what_it_shows: The Alarm Monitoring Center runs as a tenant on the Carrier's service assurance platform and watches RMU heartbeats. Procedures cover FAA outage reports by telephone, NOTAM extension and closure, and automatic work orders. The Tower contingency plan v2023 has no written fallback to daily observation if the monitoring platform is down. Outage records under 17.49 are kept in spreadsheets. Quarterly alarm system inspections are scheduled for structures that are not certified exempt

title: Tower and Fiber Infrastructure: lease management, landowner payment and lease contract records
source_system: Lease management SaaS (SYS-T1); accounts payable payment procedures; lease files
what_it_shows: About 11,800 ground-lease landowners in 22 states are paid monthly through SYS-T1 and the group ERP; SYS-T1 holds names, taxpayer IDs and bank accounts. The lease management vendor contract has no incident notice term. Bank change requests are accepted by email with a second approver. Rent from tenants is collected by ACH and wire; no card acceptance. About 26,000 route miles of dark fiber and conduit are leased under individually negotiated contracts. Tenant leases cover site access and give tenants access logs on request

title: Tower and Fiber Infrastructure: smart lock audit export and site access records
source_system: Smart lock vendor console (SYS-T2); site access requests (SYS-T1)
what_it_shows: Smart lock credentials are issued per crew, and crew members share their crew's credential; lock events are logged and exportable. Site access requests are approved in SYS-T1, with telephone authorization by the Alarm Monitoring Center as the fallback

title: Group: AI monitoring and test results, May to August 2026

MNO triage replay: 2 of 1,140 tagged alarms merged into a parent ticket. Voice agent: 0 call detail disclosures in 200 test calls; Spanish recognition errors 11% against 4%. Inspection imagery: 1.8% missed defects in 500 unflagged images. Anomaly detection: 68% of alerts confirmed
